+---
+assignees:

+position_ordinal: '8680'
+title: Correct the shell working-directory text and prove the Ask 6 scenario
+---
+## What
+Ask 6, part 3 (UPSTREAM_ASKS.md). The text the model reads says "Omit it to run in the current directory", and a model that follows it gets a refused run. Correct the text, and prove the scenario the ask describes end to end.
+
+- `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/Capabilities/Shell/Execute.swift`:
+  - The `@Guide` text of `ExecuteArguments.workingDirectory` (line 92) becomes "The directory the command runs in. Omit it to run in the session's working directory."
+  - The doc comment of `ExecuteArguments.workingDirectory` (line 88-89) names the runner default, then the process directory.
+  - The verb `description` (line 785) keeps "workingDirectory to run it somewhere else".
+- Search `Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/Capabilities/Shell/` for every other sentence that states the old fallback ("the current directory of this process", "Omit it to run in the current directory") and correct each one that is now wrong.
+- `IntegrationTests/Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolIntegrationTests/Support/ShellRunContextProbe.swift` line 24 spells the three-argument `withShell` signature; add the fourth label. `ShellBackgroundTests.swift` and `Support/ShellBackgroundRunner.swift` in the same package name `withShell()` with no labels and need no change. Do not change the behavior of the integration tests.
+- No golden pins the `tools.shell.execute` rendered text: `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/Goldens/` holds `BuilderSurface.ts.txt`, `MCPSurface.ts.txt` and `WeatherTool.ts.txt`, none of which covers the shell. So the `@Guide` change needs no golden update, and the renderer suites are not in the filter below.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] A `tools.shell.execute` call that omits `workingDirectory`, run on a bare `ShellCapability(storeDirectory:defaultWorkingDirectory:)`, prints `ShellRunner.resolvedDirectory(path:)` of the default from `pwd`.
+- [ ] The Ask 6 scenario: `root` is a temporary directory; the sandbox is `SeatbeltSandbox(options: .init(writableRoots: [root]))`; the capability has `defaultWorkingDirectory: root`; the `execute` call has no `workingDirectory` and the command `pwd`. The result carries no correction (no "outside the configured roots" text) and the output is the resolved root. (At e8c91a6 the same call is refused, because the preflight examines the process directory.)
+- [ ] The rendered `APISurface` entry for `shell.execute` (`registry.surface.entries.first { $0.path == "shell.execute" }`) contains "session's working directory" and does not contain "run in the current directory".
+- [ ] `grep -rn "Omit it to run in the current directory" Sources/` finds nothing.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Add to `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/ShellExecuteTests.swift`: `executeWithNoWorkingDirectoryRunsInTheCapabilityDefault` (bare call, no session; read `pwd` from the report or with `GetLines`), `theExecuteSurfaceNamesTheSessionWorkingDirectory`.
+- [ ] Add to `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/SandboxPreflightTests.swift` (or `SeatbeltSandboxTests.swift`, whichever already spawns `sandbox-exec`): `aPlainCommandUnderASandboxRootedAtTheDefaultIsNotRefused`, the Ask 6 scenario above. Guard it the way the other seatbelt tests are guarded when `sandbox-exec` is not available.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --filter "Shell|Sandbox"` and expect every test to pass. Then run the whole `swift test` and expect it green.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #upstream-asks #ask-6
\ No newline at end of file
